lines.text: Over two thousand years ago, a man measured the whole Earth with a stick.
In Syene, at noon on the longest day, the sun shone straight down a well.
But in Alexandria, at the same moment, a stick still cast a shadow.
If the Earth were flat, neither place would have a shadow.
So the Earth must be curved.
The shadow's angle was about seven degrees. One fiftieth of a circle.
So the Earth is about fifty times the distance between the two cities.
His answer was close to the real size. About forty thousand kilometers around.
All he needed was a stick and a shadow.
